Customer's reverse indemnity in 20.3 is properly narrow, covering only unmodified Customer-supplied material used strictly as authorized and Customer's violation of Applicable Law, with carve-outs for Vendor Technology, modification, combination or instructions. 20.5 additionally provides the fallback-level procure/modify/replace remedies with a refund of prepaid and implementation Fees (straight-line three-year basis) and bars termination of unaffected Services. The fallback super-cap of 3x annual fees is unnecessary and would be adverse to us: under 21.3 indemnification obligations are Excluded Claims and therefore uncapped. The permissive fallback exclusions (Customer modifications, combinations, specifications) are absent from 20.1, which is more favourable to us. No redline proposed.

quote: 21.1 Except for Excluded Claims, each Party's total aggregate liability arising out of or relating to this Agreement shall not exceed the greater of the Fees paid or payable by Customer during the twelve months preceding the event giving rise to the claim and USD 1,000,000. The cap is mutual and applies regardless of the form of action or number of claims.
rationale: Section 21 meets the preferred position on its material terms and therefore sits above the fallback. The cap is expressly mutual ("each Party's total aggregate liability", "The cap is mutual") and is set at the greater of Fees paid or payable in the twelve months preceding the event giving rise to the claim and USD 1,000,000. "Fees" (§ 1.5) means recurring subscription, professional services, usage and other amounts payable under an Order Form, so the 12-month basis is substantive rather than illusory. Section 21.2 excludes indirect and consequential damages mutually and confirms restoration of Customer Data, replacement services, notices and incident response are direct damages. Section 21.3 places confidentiality, data-protection and security breaches, indemnification obligations, gross negligence, wilful misconduct, fraud, and infringement of the other Party's IP wholly outside the cap, and confirms Customer's obligation to pay undisputed Fees is not damages. Section 18.2 confirms insurance does not limit Vendor's liabilities, and no warranty, indemnity or service-credit clause imposes any lower or one-sided cap. The only point short of the preferred wording is that the payment carve-out is expressed as "undisputed Fees for conforming Services" rather than all amounts due; that is a minor sub-element noted here rather than a deviation, so no redline is proposed.
ruleTitle: Limitation of liability — cap, mutuality and carve-outs

quote: 13.2 For software and Vendor Technology delivered to Customer on a paid-up basis or embedded in a Deliverable, Vendor grants Customer and its Affiliates a perpetual, irrevocable, worldwide, royalty-free, fully paid licence to use, execute, reproduce, display, perform, modify, create derivative works from, and permit contractors to support that material for Customer's business.
rationale: The licence provisions meet the preferred position in full. Section 13.1 grants the subscription/access right to "Customer, its Affiliates, and contractors acting on their behalf" for their internal business purposes, so affiliates and contractors are covered without any notice condition. Section 13.2 grants a "perpetual, irrevocable, worldwide, royalty-free, fully paid licence" for paid-up software and Vendor Technology (including material embedded in Deliverables, confirmed by Section 14.3). Section 13.3 bars Vendor from revoking or suspending a licence "except during a material uncured payment or use breach affecting the licensed item, after notice and a reasonable opportunity to cure," so the subscription licence is not revocable at will. Section 13.3 also permits Customer to transfer its licence rights to an Affiliate or successor in connection with an assignment permitted by Section 24, and Section 24.1 lets Customer assign without Vendor's consent to an Affiliate or a successor in a merger, reorganization, acquisition, or sale of substantially all assets; Section 24.4 further blocks Vendor from repricing or terminating on a Customer change of control. Section 13.4's use restrictions are narrow (reverse engineering, interference, security bypass, unlawful use) and expressly do not limit authorized security testing or use of Customer Data and output, so they do not cut back the grant. No redline is warranted.

Stating the result affirmatively rather than deleting the section preserves the numbering and avoids a dangling § 12.4 reference, so it is not a cosmetic extra.
